evidence: The hunk replaces the per-result push loop with `new Map(toolResults.map((r) => [r.id, r]))`, which drops an earlier result for a repeated id with no counter, contradicting the `unmatchedToolResults` 'counted, never dropped' invariant; the agent measured 0 live duplicates and still added `duplicateToolResults`, the proportionate move.
guidance_note: When a redesign replaces a push-per-record loop with a Map keyed by id, enumerate what a key collision now does in each direction of the join and count it in the same commit.

evidence: The badger fix rested on a one-time manual measurement against an unpinned `:latest`, and `verify` never re-checked replace-vs-append; the reviewer offered 'pin and/or extend verify' and the agent took the verify check, confirming it fails on the memory store with `Jaeger kept 2 spans...`, which catches every cause a pin would and more.
guidance_note: When a fix depends on a configuration behaviour you measured by hand, promote the throwaway probe into the stack's own verify gate in the original PR rather than recording the measurement only in a comment.

evidence: Commit 942484d shows the inline `rootsOf` closure repeated the `service.name` resource filter from `keysIn` verbatim; the fix extracts `spansOfService` and builds both `keysIn` and `rootsIn` on it.
guidance_note: Before adding a second inline selector in a test file, check whether an existing helper already performs the same filter and build on it.

evidence: F1's fix counted result-side id collisions but left `toolUses.set(block.id, ...)` overwriting silently on the request side, and with `callChildren` now driven by `conv.tools` an overwritten use loses its span; the reviewer offered a `duplicateToolUses` counter as one remedy and the agent added it while correctly declining recovery, since two spans sharing `tool:<id>` collapse under badger anyway (the agent's argument follows from the PR's own span-id scheme).
guidance_note: When fixing a key-collision gap on one side of a join, sweep the symmetric map on the other side of the same join before pushing.

evidence: F1's fix (2af79c2) added `duplicateToolResults` with only `attribution.test.ts` setting it to 0 and no test that feeds a duplicate; the agent added `duplicateToolResultSession` asserting count 1 and last-result-wins.
guidance_note: A counter added to answer a review finding ships with a test that drives the counted shape and asserts the count, in the same fix commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the README badger paragraph restating 'memory store appends ... Badger replaces it' was in the original PR (round-0 hunk), not in 942484d, which touched only the test file; the paragraph both restated the stack.sh measurement and named stack.sh as its owner, and b5334a9 trimmed it to the consequence.

evidence: F2's fix (6594b9d) added `verify_replaces` and updated `verify`'s usage text but left the README 'Run `verify` after every `up`' paragraph describing only the arrival check; b5334a9 rewrote it to name both checks, as the diff shows.
guidance_note: When a fix changes what a command checks, grep the docs for every description of that command and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The F1 fix's loop `if (resultOf.has(r.id)) duplicateToolResults++` counts repeats of unmatched ids too, so two results for an unrequested id read as 1 duplicate plus 2 unmatched; the agent confirmed this and restricted the count with `&& toolUses.has(r.id)`, verified by mutation.
guidance_note: When adding a second anomaly counter beside an existing one, write the case table of which records each counts and make them partition before pushing.

evidence: This is the same missing test as F5, plus the correct observation that `ToolCallSpec` cannot build two results for one id, so a hand-written transcript is needed; c954793 adds it and also caught the agent's own vacuous first partition test.
guidance_note: A counter added to answer a review finding ships with a test that drives the counted shape and asserts the count, in the same fix commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the fixtures.ts per-block seconds comment is original PR content (round 0 already describes the 'per-block sub-minute timestamps'), and 942484d did not touch it; with `sec = k` 0-based, 60 blocks reach second 59, so 'sixty' was off by one.
guidance_note: When a comment states a numeric threshold derived from an index, compute it from the code's base (0- or 1-based) before writing it.

evidence: F4's fix (a7b4127) added `duplicateToolUses` with no test, one round after F5/F9 required exactly that test for its result-side twin; the agent concedes 'did not mirror the test I had just been made to write' and adds `duplicateToolUseSession` with tree-level assertions confirmed by mutation.
guidance_note: When a reviewer has just required a test for one counter, apply that requirement to every new counter you add in the next fix without waiting to be asked.

evidence: The 'so nothing is lost' comment in spans.ts contradicted the loss that F4's fix documented in calls.ts, and the agent fixed it in 19142b4; the graft-misattribution premise was wrong, because `forest.ts` `indexTools` does the same last-wins `owner.set(b.id, ...)` over the same blocks, and 720cebb pins `spawnedAtCall === 1` alongside `callIndex === 1`, so the proposed guard would be a no-op.
guidance_note: When a fix documents a new loss case in one module, grep the consuming module for comments asserting completeness ('nothing is lost', 'every') and correct them in the same commit.

evidence: This duplicates F11: `duplicateToolUses` from a7b4127 had no test that drives a collision; it was answered by the same 720cebb fixture.
guidance_note: When a reviewer has just required a test for one counter, apply that requirement to every new counter you add in the next fix without waiting to be asked.

evidence: The `duplicateToolResults` doc comment written in the F8 partition fix ('AND has a tool_use') claimed the result is one 'the analysis does not carry', but the `arrivals` loop prices every tool_result block, so the comment was false; the reviewer's framing of the double-count as a bug is weaker, since both blocks entered context, and the agent fixed the comment rather than deduping arrivals, which is one of the two remedies the reviewer offered. The packet cannot show whether a real duplicate tool_result would be two billed sends or a writer artifact, so the 'honest number' claim is reasoned, not verified.
guidance_note: When a doc comment says a record has no further effect on 'the analysis', trace every consumer of the raw records (here `arrivals`) before writing the scope claim.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 'every span the first export sent keeps its trace' was in the original test (round-0 F3 hunk), and dde13ef touched only the README; `traceIdOf` is stamped once per export, so the within-domain comparison could not fail, and the agent replaced it with cross-export and cross-domain assertions confirmed by mutating `traceIdOf`.
guidance_note: Before committing a test, name a plausible broken implementation it would catch; if none exists in reachable code, the assertion is vacuous.

evidence: The flag is a false positive in its cause: `[...toolUses]` ordering by Map insertion comes from the original join redesign, not from any fix, and dde13ef was README-only. `Map.set` on an existing key keeps its position, so a collided id sorts out of order, which the agent reproduced (`['Read','Bash']`) and fixed by sorting `callChildren` by `tStart`.
guidance_note: When output order matters, derive it from the data (timestamps) rather than from a Map's insertion order.

narrative: The round-0 Map-keyed join fix (F1) seeded most of the later review: the symmetric request-side gap (F4), missing tests (F5/F9), overlapping counters (F8), and then F4's own counter repeated the missing-test gap (F11/F13) and left a contradicting comment (F12). F8's redefinition comment overclaimed in round 3 (F14). Round 2 was entirely fix-caused, and the PR hit the 5-round cap with its head unreviewed. The agent's pushbacks (F4 recovery, F12 guard, F14 arrivals) were checked with tests or traced mechanisms and held up.
guidance_observations: Each fix added a new counter or comment without the test and sweep the previous round had just required, so the same lesson was taught twice (F5/F9 then F11/F13).
A fix to one side of a symmetric join should sweep the other side and the downstream consumers (spans.ts comments, arrivals) before pushing, not after the next round.
The agent's practice of settling disputed premises with mutation-verified tests rather than argument was effective and should be kept.
